A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adaptive canonicalization framework and retain identifiable matching methods, theorems and experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph and point-cloud classification results in Tables 1–3, with additional implementation comparisons and rotation-generalization experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds ablations, CIFAR classification, ShapeNet segmentation, computational measurements and stability analyses.

M1.justification: The original prior-maximization framework remains, but v2 adds crop-and-resize canonicalization (E.5) and a segmentation variant that selects transformations by minimizing entropy summed over points (G.10). The spectral implementation is also reported with Jk-dimensional rotations after padding, versus Mk-dimensional rotations before padding in v1. These are substantive procedural extensions beyond expanded explanations of the existing search.

E1.justification: V2 adds natural-image classification on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and point-level part segmentation on ShapeNet, extending both domain and prediction-task coverage. The original toy, TUDataset, OGB and ModelNet40 evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original benchmark tables is retained. New comparisons introduce unmodified PointNet++ and RSCNN alongside their adaptive variants in Table 10, and a vanilla pretrained ResNet-18 control in Table 11. Reusing existing point-cloud comparators on ShapeNet is chiefly a coverage extension.

E3.justification: Original Appendix F protocols remain, while v2 adds frozen-backbone classifier training on CIFAR, category-mean-IoU segmentation evaluation, controlled sensitivity sweeps and consecutive-epoch rotation measurements on 1,500 training examples. Its spectral implementation also replaces the previously stated maximum-eigenvalue-scaled dyadic bands with boundaries anchored at 2. This reported setting revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained G.1–G.3 analyses, v2 tests uniform versus dyadic bands, alternative graph shift operators and additional point-cloud backbones. It adds hyperparameter sensitivity, runtime/parameter comparisons, canonical-rotation stability and a visualization of 20 canonicalized chairs (G.4–G.9), substantially expanding investigation of design choices and behavior.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly supplies ± uncertainties for augmentation, canonicalization and adaptive-canonicalization rows that previously had point estimates only. G.6 specifies ten independent CIFAR runs. The existing TUDataset ten-split reporting practice remains; increased run counts for retained ModelNet40 results are not documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 5–7 retain their results. Table 3 revises AC-PointNet from 81.3 to 81.1, AC-DGCNN from 91.7 to 91.6, and augmentation baselines from 76.4/89.3 to 75.8/89.0 under the retained stated protocol. Tables 8–13 and Figures 2–4 add substantial new findings, including CIFAR gains and mixed segmentation performance: AC-DGCNN scores 80.9 versus VN-DGCNN's 81.4.

T1.justification: The principal continuity, symmetry and universal-approximation theorems and proofs remain unchanged. V2 adds auxiliary volume-retaining assumptions and a cited concentration inequality (Definition 21, Lemma 22), an epsilon-plus-search-error approximation argument, and a formal continuity check for truncation. V1's Appendix D automorphism derivation is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statement and conclusion retain the same central claims: network-dependent canonicalization, continuity, symmetry preservation, universal approximation and superior classification performance. Additional applications and supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations concerning spectral normalization, band selection, backbone robustness, crop selection and stabilization of canonical poses, plus an argument about specialization versus separately learned canonicalizers. G.10 explicitly leaves continuity of the entropy-based segmentation variant unresolved. The earlier regression and per-class optimization-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: The rewritten tutorial adds pseudocode, explicit candidate counts of 32 for graphs and 50 for point clouds, projection/Riemannian refinement options, and fuller spectral and cropping instructions. New experiments disclose frozen-backbone training and runtime/parameter information. Conversely, v1's explicit instruction against differentiating through refinement and its node-level construction equation are omitted; Appendix F's existing hardware and hyperparameter details remain.

R1.justification: A new main-text related-work section and expanded Appendix A substantially develop comparisons with energy-based canonicalization, weighted canonicalization/frame averaging and test-time transformation search. Newly discussed works include Shumaylov et al., Schmidt and Stober, and Basu et al. V2 also adds cognitive-psychology positioning while elaborating distinctions from previously cited Kaba and Dym.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes and rewrites the supporting narrative: it adds a main related-work section, subdivides Appendix A's comparisons, and rebuilds Appendix E as a practitioner tutorial with consolidated classification and optimization explanations. It removes the appendix roadmap and shortens G.2, while largely preserving the main theoretical exposition.

P2.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1, Tables 8–13 and Figures 2–4, introducing sensitivity plots, a training-stability curve and canonicalized point-cloud examples. Table 3 gains a provenance caption and source markers, and existing tables are relocated or reflowed. The original framework schematic remains.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support that v1 lacked: G.4–G.9 examine design choices, sensitivity, computational cost and canonicalization behavior. Broader task evaluations, newly reported uncertainty and fuller implementation and related-work discussion improve assessment of generality and reproducibility. Some implementation details are lost, and segmentation continuity remains unresolved, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
